To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we devise a sample-optimal asymptotic test and a sample-optimal practical non-asymptotictest for the known central ranking case, (2) we devise a practical asymptotic test for the unknown centralranking case and (3) we show that our tests scale well with the number of rankings to be compared and are robust to the presence of outliers.

(i) for known central ranking, we provide an asymptotically optimal and a sample optimal non-asymptotically optimal identity test; and (ii) for unknown central ranking we provide an asymptotic identity test that is sample-optimal in the limit of large sample sizes.

We provide a sample-optimal test for identity testing of Mallows models with a known central ranking, and we show that the same test also works for an unknown central ranking with a small bias that exponentially decents in the sample size.
